quote.text: Doubt is not a pleasant condition, but certainty is absurd.
quote.author: Voltaire, letter to Frederick William of Prussia (1770)

stories.kicker: The World · The Black Sea Reprisal
stories.headline: Ukraine Burns a Port, and the Price of Bread Twitches
stories.dek: An overnight strike on Novorossiysk — Russia's main Black Sea naval base and its largest grain gate — left four warships damaged and two export terminals dark. Chicago wheat jumped three per cent. But Moscow is already rerouting cargo, and Kyiv, on an American request, left the Chevron-owned oil terminal untouched: a reprisal calibrated as much as it was fierce.

stories.kicker: Technology · The Open Frontier, With a Lock
stories.headline: A 2.4-Trillion-Parameter Model Goes Free — Under a Licence That Bars Half the West
stories.dek: Alibaba has posted the weights of Qwen3.8-Max, a claimed-frontier model, for anyone to download — then attached a custom revenue-share licence that, on one reading, forbids users in the US, EU, UK and Korea from even downloading it. Export controls slowed the hardware; the capability is now being given away.

stories.headline: Reassurance, by the Minute
stories.dek: India isn't secularising as it modernises. It is platformising faith — and a generation's loneliness has just been floated toward the stock exchange. This month a live-astrology app became the country's newest unicorn. The market, not the state, is filling a mental-health void the size of a nation.

stories.kicker: Singapore · The Licence and the Seat
stories.headline: Struck Off as a Lawyer, the Opposition Chief Keeps His Seat
stories.dek: The Court of Three Judges struck Pritam Singh from the roll of advocates and solicitors on Thursday — the professional coda to a conviction already litigated. It ends his legal career and touches neither his parliamentary seat nor his party post: a symbolic escalation with limited mechanics behind it.

stories.headline: A Record Land Price, Set by a Single Bidder — and a Resale Market Drifting the Other Way
stories.dek: The bull case and the bear case are the same fact: one developer paid a new benchmark for a waterfront plot that four to six were meant to chase. Read against a Q2 index barely positive and a June sales slump, it describes a market held up by scarce land, not broad demand.

stories.headline: Two 8K 360 Cameras Launch in One Week — Only One Has a Price You Can Pay
stories.dek: DJI put the Osmo 360 II on stage on 13 August, a day after Insta360's X6 went on sale. The DJI wins the spec sheet — 8K60, replaceable lenses, a bigger battery — but it launched China-first with no price in any market. For a buy-once reader, the paradox: the better camera is the one you can't yet buy.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · The Flagship Season Opens
stories.headline: Bowers & Wilkins Redraws the 800 at Sixty — the First Full Redesign Since 2021
stories.dek: The fifth-generation 800 Series Diamond reaches market on 9 September, from US$15,000 to US$65,000 a pair. Final pricing and first-listen reviews have landed; the diamond tweeter now sits in a revised turbine head. The measurement crowd, as ever, is unmoved — which is exactly the debate a buy-once buyer should read.

stories.kicker: Screen & Sound · The Record and the Asterisk
stories.headline: The Biggest Box-Office Summer Ever Crosses Four Billion — Read the Ticket Price First
stories.dek: A Spider-Man opening for the ages and a still-dominant Nolan epic pushed the summer domestic box office past US$4bn, a new record. But the "biggest ever" leans on record ticket prices and premium-format surcharges — and the film driving it has the widest critic-audience gap of its franchise.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Hinge Age
stories.headline: Girls Quit Sport at Exactly Your Daughter's Age — and the Fix Isn't "Try Harder"
stories.dek: As Term 4 CCA renewals come round, the research is unusually specific: eleven to thirteen is when girls disengage from sport, and reaching puberty predicts dropping individual sports in particular. The protective move is social, not motivational — keep her in a team through the awkward window. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · The Record and the Long Bond
stories.headline: Stocks Set a Record on a Mild Inflation Print — the Real Signal Is in the Long Bond
stories.dek: The S&P 500 closed above 7,800 for the first time as July's CPI came in soft. But the same week's Treasury auctions priced money at its dearest in a generation — the 30-year the priciest in 25 years, the 10-year the highest yield since 2007. Records on top; higher-for-longer underneath. Explanation, not advice.

stories.headline: The Outlaw Airwaves: Fifty-Nine Years Ago This Weekend, DJs Became Criminals
stories.dek: Last week's descent sent you to the far end of the dial to listen. This one holds the same wire from the other end — the act of transmitting. Pressing "receive" is legal everywhere; pressing "transmit" is a crime almost everywhere. That gap is the whole story. Culture, history and the law — never a how-to.

stories.kicker: Fitness · The Number That Changes at Forty
stories.headline: It Isn't Your Step Count — It's How Much Protein a Shrinking Muscle Needs
stories.dek: The dietary protein figure most people carry — 0.8 grams per kilo — was set for the average sedentary adult, and it's wrong for a 40-something losing about a per cent of muscle a year. The recalibrated target is 1.0 to 1.2, paired with resistance training. General guidance, not medical advice.

stories.headline: An F1 Sprint Weekend to Lock, and a Japanese Autumn Worth Booking Flights For
stories.dek: Singapore's October stacks a first-ever F1 Sprint against a run of sold-out shows; December brings a family-perfect Nutcracker. In Japan, Ghibli Park adds Porco Rosso's seaplane and the koyo windows reward booking the rooms now. Lock the tickets before the diaries fill.
